title: Gripper, cutting apparatus and method for cutting a product

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
features.note: This reference describes a gripper with a suction device, not a magnetic gripper with a housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes.

features.item: A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
features.note: This reference describes a suction device, not a magnetic gripper with a displaceable magnet.

features.item: Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
features.note: This reference describes a suction device with sealing devices and contact surfaces, not pole shoes attached to a housing.

features.item: Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: This reference describes a suction device, not a magnetic gripper with pole shoes guiding a magnetic field.

features.item: A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
features.note: This reference describes a suction device and does not mention any magnetic components or specific angles of contact surfaces relative to a displacement direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
features.note: This reference describes a suction gripper, not a magnetic gripper with the specified components and contact surface angle.

features.item: A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
features.note: This reference describes a suction gripper system that grips a product using vacuum, not a magnetic gripper system using magnetic force.

features.item: Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
features.note: This reference describes a gripper with a suction device but does not specify a housing extending along a longitudinal axis with a parallel displacement direction for a magnet.

features.item: Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
features.note: This reference describes a suction device, not a magnetic gripper with pole shoes or active structures for directing a magnetic field.

features.item: An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: This reference describes sealing devices like blade edges, beads, or sealing lips, but not an active structure with a bevel defining a specific angle with a workpiece contact surface in the context of magnetic gripping.

features.item: An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: This reference describes suction sections and sealing devices, some of which may have tips or claws, but not an active structure with multiple projections for directing a magnetic field.

features.item: Adjacent first and second projections with a recess between them, recess depth or length deviating by at most 25% from projection length.
features.note: This reference describes suction sections and sealing devices, but not adjacent projections with a recess between them with specific dimensional relationships for magnetic field direction.

features.item: A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
features.note: This reference describes a gripper for gripping a product using suction, but does not mention a magnetic gripper or a specific positioning device for a ferromagnetic workpiece.

features.item: First and second pole shoes where the magnet in gripping position makes the first pole shoe act as north pole and second as south pole.
features.note: This reference describes a suction device, not a magnetic gripper with pole shoes acting as north and south poles.

features.item: A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
features.note: This reference describes a suction device, not a magnetic gripper with an electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically displaceable magnet.

features.item: A position sensor detecting gripping position and/or release position, or a workpiece sensor detecting the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: This reference mentions monitoring suction power and vacuum to detect leakage flows, but not a position sensor for gripping/release or a workpiece sensor for ferromagnetic workpieces.

features.item: Housing with a receptacle for receiving a workpiece sensor and/or a supply line.
features.note: This reference describes a gripper with a suction device but does not explicitly mention a housing with a receptacle for a workpiece sensor or a supply line in the context of a magnetic gripper.

features.item: A manipulator interface on the magnetic gripper for attaching to a manipulator.
features.note: This reference describes a gripper for a cutting apparatus but does not mention a manipulator interface for a magnetic gripper.

features.item: Housing portion designed to suppress magnetic field escape, or a shielding device to at least partially prevent magnetic field escape.
features.note: This reference describes a suction device and does not mention any magnetic components or shielding for magnetic field escape.

features.item: At least one projection with length deviating by at most 25% from the thickness of the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: This reference describes sealing devices and mechanical gripping elements like tips or claws, but not projections with specific length relationships to a ferromagnetic workpiece thickness for magnetic gripping.

features.item: A receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.
features.note: This reference does not explicitly describe a receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.

features.item: A bevel angle of 15° to 75° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: This reference describes blade edges and their slopes, but not an active structure with a bevel defining a specific angle with a workpiece contact surface in the context of magnetic gripping.

features.item: A bevel angle of 40° to 60° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: This reference describes blade edges and their slopes, but not an active structure with a bevel defining a specific angle with a workpiece contact surface in the context of magnetic gripping.

claims.note: This reference describes a gripper that uses suction for gripping a product, not a magnetic gripper for ferromagnetic workpieces.
This reference describes a suction device for gripping, not a displaceable magnet for gripping and releasing a ferromagnetic workpiece.
This reference describes sealing devices and suction sections, not pole shoes that guide a magnetic field to a workpiece contact surface.
This reference does not describe a contact surface angle in relation to a displacement direction, as it pertains to a suction gripper, not a magnetic gripper.
This reference describes a suction gripper for food products, not a magnetic gripper, and does not mention any contact surface angle or displacement direction.
This reference describes a suction gripper, not a magnetic gripper with a housing extending along a longitudinal axis.
This reference describes a suction gripper, not a magnetic gripper with a displacement direction aligned parallel to a longitudinal axis.
This reference describes a suction gripper, not a magnetic gripper with pole shoes having an active structure for directing a magnetic field portion.
This reference describes grippers that use suction and mechanical elements, not magnetic grippers with active structures and bevels.
This reference describes grippers that use suction and mechanical elements, not magnetic grippers with active structures and bevels defining a bevel angle.
This reference describes grippers that use suction and mechanical elements, not magnetic grippers with active structures and bevels defining a bevel angle within a specified range.
This reference describes grippers that use suction and mechanical elements, not magnetic grippers with active structures having projections for directing a magnetic field.
This reference describes suction sections and sealing devices, but not specifically a plurality of projections including at least a first and second projection.
This reference describes multiple suction sections, but does not explicitly state that two specific projections are adjacent to one another.
This reference describes recesses forming suction sections, but not a recess specifically between a first and second projection of an active structure.
This reference does not disclose any specific dimensional relationships between recesses and projections, let alone a deviation of at most 25%.
This reference describes a suction gripper for food products, not a magnetic gripper with a positioning device for ferromagnetic workpieces.
This reference describes a suction gripper for food products and does not mention pole shoes or magnetic gripping.
This reference describes a suction gripper for food products and does not mention magnets, north poles, or south poles.
This reference describes a suction gripper and does not mention a magnet displaceable between gripping and release positions.
This reference describes a suction gripper for food products, not a magnetic gripper, and does not mention a position sensor for detecting gripping or release positions.
This reference describes a suction gripper for food products, not a magnetic gripper, and does not mention a workpiece sensor for detecting a ferromagnetic workpiece.
This reference describes a suction gripper and does not mention a housing with a receptacle for a workpiece sensor or a supply line.
This reference describes a gripper for cutting apparatus and does not mention a manipulator interface for attaching the gripper to a manipulator.
This reference describes a gripper that uses suction, not magnetism, and therefore does not discuss suppressing magnetic fields.
This reference describes a gripper that uses suction, not magnetism, and therefore does not discuss a shielding device for magnetic fields.
This reference describes a suction gripper system, not a magnetic gripper system.
This reference describes a suction gripper, not a magnetic gripper, and does not mention a ferromagnetic workpiece.
This reference describes a vacuum gripper for food products, not a magnetic gripper for ferromagnetic workpieces. There is no mention of magnets, gripping positions, or magnetic forces.
This reference describes a vacuum gripper for food products, not a magnetic gripper for ferromagnetic workpieces. There is no mention of magnets, release positions, or magnetic forces.
This reference describes a vacuum gripper for food products, not a magnetic gripper for ferromagnetic workpieces. There is no mention of projections or ferromagnetic workpieces.
This reference describes a vacuum gripper for food products. There is no mention of a receptacle in the form of a groove.

overall.why: This reference describes a suction gripper for food products, which is fundamentally different from a magnetic gripper system. None of the subject invention's features related to magnetic gripping are disclosed.
